entry.title: Motivational Speech #769 (From the iterating.com Archives Which Do Not Exist)
entry.summary: You never correct a fool. You ever hear that? Never. Want…
entry.content:
You never correct a fool.

You ever hear that?

Never.

Want to know why?

Because the fool will get angry.

Angrier.

Generally fools get angry easy.

Grrr.

And, with correction, they only get angrier.

Bitter(er).

Now, as a guy who likes to correct, who's left?

Non-fools.

Those who are willing to learn.

To be corrected.

Where warranted of course.

Correct those lovely folks, please.

Unless you're a fool.

Which, let's face it, you might be.

Statistically quite likely.

Being corrected by a fool is next level sheet.

Ever have that happen?

Final level.

But you.

You?

You're doing great.

Wouldn't change a thing!

Keep up the great work!

entry.title: I'm Going to Duel Him Lefthanded
entry.summary: There was this famous experiment. Maybe not so famous. But listen.
entry.content:
There was this famous experiment.

Maybe not so famous.

But listen.

I gotta point to make.

And it ain't on the top of your head!

It was an experiment in some class in some school somewhere in the world.

And the class was divided into two groups.

Each group had the same goal:

To make the best pot or something like that.

Details don't matter.

The first group had to spend all their time on making one pot.

The perfect pot.

The second had to make a pot a day for a month or however long it went.

And guess who won?

Second group.

The results showed that by iterating over and over again, you got a better pot.

More reps.

More bites.

More chances.

Sure, you make a lot of bad pots, but you get the best ones out of the batch, too.

And this is part of the problem with how we do things growing up.

Perfection is rewarded.

And usually for just one try.

You don't get to do-over papers and exams (typically).

Short-term memorization is the standard.

Regurgitate.

Spew.

100%.

This is a horrible way to get great at something.

Other than in regurgitation.

And spewing.

You'll fit right in here.

Of course.

When I was learning muay thai, it was obvious my front leg (left) was weak.

Now I had have monster hands.

Knees that would make my partner quit holding pads mid-round.

But front leg.

Was weak.

WEAK!

So I over-trained it.

Over-emphasized it.

It was a mission.

Learned to love that dang leg.

Turning weakness into something else.

Left side?

Strong side!

Something fun.

Soon, after many, many, reps, it became a strength.

A favorite.

Because it took work.

Because it was weak.

Because it cost time.

Because it got better.

Because I earned it.

If I only kicked once, it would suck. 

And it did.

No matter how much I planned the kick.

Of course, a left kick to the liver now would still put someone in the ER.

Me.

So iterating for me has changed.

The reps have changed.

Fingers.

My thumbs are going to be huge.

Musings.

Ideas.

But the model hasn't.

And it's one I learned late.

Like a lot of things.

Wissmart is often delayed.

But never denied.

God bless you all.

Most of you.

Work on your weaknesses.

Making failing fun.

And remember, you are the pot.

You get to make yourself every single day.

Every other day.

A week maybe.

The point is, you're the pot.

Have fun, left kicks.

entry.title: 'Til The Smoke Clears Out
entry.summary: I've talked before about Kintsugi. Beauty in the broken. This idea,…
entry.content:
I've talked before about Kintsugi.

Beauty in the broken.

This idea, or rather art, where you take something broken (like pottery or you) and turn it into something more beautiful.

In the pottery's case this is done by gluing it back together with glue made with gold.

Feature the scars. 

Don't hide them.

I don't know how we fix you.

I got gold glue here somewhere.

It's a wonderful idea.

One I resonate with.

But I recently learned of another.

Antifragile.

It's the worst name for the best idea I've heard in a long time.

The cursed double negative.

This idea that not only do you recover, better than ever, from what breaks you.

But that you flourish in the chaos.

During it.

That you prosper in the sheet.

"Were you in the sheet?"

"Yeah. I was in the sheet."

It reminds me of Rudy's poem:

If you can keep your head when all about you are losing theirs and blaming it on you.

Ooh, that one's good. 

If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster, and treat those two imposters just the same.

Man, that might be even better.

Or watch the things you gave your life to, broken, and stoop and build 'em up with worn out tools.

This is some of the best stuff.

I think Kippy had it.

The right idea.

Mindset.

I keep thinking of Hulk and Wolverine.

Stronger, strongest, in the fight.

During the fight.

Don't.

Just.

Survive.

Mother mother.

Win.

Force your heart, nerve, and sinew to serve your turn long after they are gone.

There are stories of men fighting wars who have had parts of their heads gone and yet, impossibly, still continue to fight.

They didn't know they were deed.

Because they simply did not allow it.

The fight must go on.

The fighter must, too.

Now, I hope you aren't at war.

Cabeza intact.

But there's no more time for the pity party you've been throwing.

It's time for a different kind of party.

Be that mother motherin' life form they find on some faraway (thought lifeless) planet.

How in the world is this thing still alive?

Hulk smash.

Nate, hit me.

🎤

Til the roof comes off, 

Til the lights go out

Til my leg give out

Can't shut my mouth.

...

I'ma rip this sheet

Til my bone collapse.

🦴

At your highest, when the roof comes off.

At your best, when the lights go out.

At your strongest, when your leg (singular) give out.

At your toughest, when the bone collapse.

Rip this sheet.

Snikt.

entry.title: Hang Up The Mudgeons
entry.summary: Reality checks sometimes bounce. Sometimes, they clear. There comes a time…
entry.content:
Reality checks sometimes bounce.

Sometimes, they clear.

There comes a time though.

When a curmudgeon's gotta hang up his mudgeons.

He's gotta just say thank you.

What is a mudgeon?

I learned a new term the other day.

One I've lived and live but never knew there was a term for.

PTG.

Post Traumatic Growth.

Focus on the G.

Something sheety happens.

And you transform.

Into something, into someone, better.

Like a mother motherin' snake doc.

Now, I ain't perfect.

But I kinda thought I was.

I kinda did.

You kinda did.

Boy, did I get a reckoning.

To the bone.

Humble pie was served.

That sheet came on a big sheet.

Here's the weird part.

The pie tasted good.

This is some good pie!

🥧

I needed it.

Sure, it made me skinny then fat(ish), took my muscles, made me age, but I am still here, y'all.

Still ticking.

No tocking.

I still walk around like old (young) me.

But I know that's just me fighting a ghost.

I want to tell you how great grateful I am, but it's hard to say.

What doesn't keel you, makes you stronger.

Embrace adversities.

Revel in chaos.

Embrace the suck.

That's a lot of hugging.

Now I'll be the first to tell you, I ain't gone through sheet compared to a lot of you.

But there's another way to go after the PT.

You don't have to go SD.

Don't stress disorder, learn to welcome it.

It has no idea who it's messing with.

Welcome to the Chungle.

Invite it in (it's coming in anyways, might as well welcome the beech).

And then serve it some pie.

🥧

You dirty mother...

Thank you.

You know where you are?

You're in the Chungle, baby.

You're gonna live.

entry.title: ...That's Funny...
entry.summary: One thing I noticed... About really bright minds... Is when you…
entry.content:
One thing I noticed...

About really bright minds...

Is when you ask them a tough question...

...They pause...

Before answering...

You can see the gears turning...

...⚙...

I've known idiots who consider this low wattage.

But they're idiots for a reason.

Idiots.

Idiots respond so fast they cut the question off.

They think it's smart to do so.

But it's not.

It's the opposite.

Idiots.

So anyways, I'm going to start pausing when I answer now.

You have to do it almost to the point of discomfort.

The pause that is.

Stone faced.

Eyes distant.

You own those seconds.

Then wait a little bit longer.

Wait too long.

Then, and only then, answer.

Ideally, you'd do so with a poignant response.

Well thought out and pre-reasoned.

Several iterations inside your head.

But this is the ideal.

Not necessary.

The necessary part is to look like you're doing it.

...I might have that all wrong...

...

...

...

...But don't we all?...

🔄

entry.title: Where Are You Going, Pilgrim?
entry.summary: Say your arse got to Plymouth Rock. Back in the day.
entry.content:
Say your arse got to Plymouth Rock.

Back in the day.

How far you moving out west?

You making it to the other ocean?

Or you stopping somewhere?

Somewhere in Nebraska.

Idaho, maybe?

Pocatello!!!

Or would you stay put?

It's dark in New Amsterdam.

Now, I ain't no pilgrim, Pilgrim.

Or am I?

[Looks up dictionary term:]

A pilgrim is a person who takes a long journey to a sacred or holy place for religious reasons.

This sounds like me.

Or, at least, I'd like it to.

I'd like it to sound like me.

Now, I ain't Chon Wang.

But I dig the Wild West.

Just wasn't for me.

Here you go.

Didn't find God there.

Almost lost Him.

Almost.

🙏

Your whole life is a pilgrimage.

If you think about it.

If you do it right.

A (hopefully) long journey.

To the most sacred places.

In full faith.

May we all get to where we're going.

I'd probably stop in Kansas.

entry.content:

You ever think about that?

LOL.

Minding our own.

Well, you will probably win, then.

It's fooked up but that's why we're here.

Remember gluten free?

The thing is, most of it doesn't seem like a big deal.

So we shrug it off.

But it is.

I'm only inconvenienced.

It is the biggest deal.

Does this have seed oil?

Oh for the love of...

entry.title: All I've Got Is An Autograph
entry.summary: I bought a book the other day. You don't read. You…
entry.content:
I bought a book the other day.

You don't read.

You barely listen.

Hey, it happens.

I like to buy ones you can't find digitally.

Oldish ones.

Obscurish ones.

Hidden gems.

And so I found one I already own, online but in analog form, and ordered it.

Two is one.

And it came in good shape.

Always a win.

And, surprisingly, it was autographed by the author.

Now if you buy a lot of tangible books intangibly, you'll notice this.

Signed copies.

Unmentioned.

At bargain rates.

Often, they are personalized.

To Milton,

Reach for the stars!

And sometimes, they're autographed by, not the author, but the gifter.

I don't really think of individual copies of books having their own unique stories but they do.

They have unreplicable tales.

Outside of its internal contents.

It has its own external contexts.

What was a print run of X number is really a unique 1 of 1.

With a story all its own.

And I suppose we're all like that.

Massive print runs, but really a one of one.

A unique take on an old story.

With our own personalized, autographed, version.

Hey Numbnuts,

Don't screw this up.

Love,

Al

[Thinking while staring at you intently.]

I'll give you...three dollars.

📕

🐆

entry.title: Quill Over Key
entry.summary: I got nothing to say. Yeah right. I don't. Nothing. Nada.
entry.content:
I got nothing to say.

Yeah right.

I don't.

Nothing.

Nada.

Zilch.

When I write, by hand, with pen and paper, it's awesome.

Wonderful.

But there's a limit.

I'm limited by how fast, or slow, I can write.

I have to be deliberate.

Thoughts move a bit faster than my penmanship.

I have to slow down.

And so I learned to love typing.

I can almost type stream of consciousness here.

Meaning I can type as I think.

Before I think even.

Lord help us.

Just typing words out first to make a thought appear later.

And so when I handwrite, the output is thoughtful, considered, and concise.

When I type, woo boy, you get this.

Rambles.

It occurs to me, as such things do, that this musings column has halted my hand written stuff.

My offline musings.

Best musings are done offline.

All this (pointing to iterating) is a bit absurd.

Agreed?

Mmhmm.

Time to pick up that feather.

entry.title: Unreasoned Within Reason
entry.summary: I want to teach you a new term. Orthogonal bets. Oar.
entry.content:
I want to teach you a new term.

Orthogonal bets.

Oar.

Thog.

Gonal.

Now, it may not be new to you, but if it is, it is.

Orthogonal is a fancy way to say 90 degrees.

Perpendicular.

Which is also fancy.

X goes up.

Y goes right.

Never the two shall cross.

I suppose they do at you, though.

You are the cross(roads).

I read it in two ways.

Maybe more.

One is if everybody zigging.

You zag.

Everyone zagging.

You zig.

You dig?

And if all you do is zag.

Maybe somethings you zig.

Or if zig, then zag.

If you Zig Ziglar.

Try Zag Zaglir.

You can call it a hedge, I suppose.

Hedge on your life.

If you're into that.

But I really think this is where all the asymmetric stuff is.

The fun stuff.

If everyone is going one way.

Or if you are.

Maybe you go the other way.

You turn right.

Or left.

Not all the time, now.

All the time gets you in trouble.

Just enough.

To keep things interesting.

Keep things fresh.

If all you do is digital.

Be a little analog.

And versa vice.

All you do is highways.

Take the local route.

Like Bob Frost said.

Take the road less traveled.

Makes all the difference.

Start making orthogonal bets.

Don't make it the main thing.

Unless you want to.

Just enough to be unreasonable.

Within reason.

"Are you going to help me or not?"

"Alright, alright, alright!

I'll tell you what to do:

Go that way.

Really fast.

If something gets in your way,

Turn."

⛷

👈

[Watching you ragdoll down a mountain].

Alright!

Now, turn!!!

🎩
